label: ass:filtering
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:filtering}
The functions
\[
 b:\mathbb R^d\times U\to\mathbb R^d,
 \qquad
 \sigma:\mathbb R^d\times U\to\mathbb R^{d\times r},
 \qquad
 h:\mathbb R^d\times U\to\mathbb R^m
\]
are Borel measurable.  There is a constant $K\ge1$ such that, for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$ and $v\in U$,
\begin{align}
 &\left\lvert b(x,v)-b(y,v)\right\rvert+\left\lVert \sigma(x,v)-\sigma(y,v)\right\rVert
   \le K\left\lvert x-y\right\rvert,
   \label{eq:filtering-lipschitz}\\
 &\left\lvert b(x,v)\right\rvert+\left\lVert \sigma(x,v)\right\rVert+\left\lvert h(x,v)\right\rvert
   \le K(1+\left\lvert x\right\rvert+\left\lvert v\right\rvert).
   \label{eq:filtering-growth}
\end{align}

label: lem:flow-estimates
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Flow estimates

title: Proof
body_md:
First, it is easy to verify:
	\begin{align*}
		&\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}
		\sup_{t\le a\le s}|\Phi_{t,a}(x)|^q\\
		&\quad\le C_q\bigl(1+|x|^q+k^{q/2}\bigr)
		+C_q\int_t^s
		\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}
		\sup_{t\le r\le a}|\Phi_{t,r}(x)|^q\,\mathrm d a.
	\end{align*}
Then,	Gronwall's inequality yields
	\[
	\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}|\Phi_{t,s}(x)|^q
	\le C_q\bigl(1+|x|^q+k^{q/2}\bigr)
	\le C_{k,q}\left\langle x\right\rangle^q.
	\]
This	proves \eqref{eq:flow-state-moment}.
	
Denote
	\[
	B_s:=\chi_s^tD_xb(\Phi_{t,s}(x),u_s),
	\quad
	C_s^\nu:=\chi_s^tD_x\sigma^\nu(\Phi_{t,s}(x),u_s),
	\]
where $\sigma^\nu$  denotes the $\nu$th column of the diffusion matrix  $\sigma$. 
Then, we have, 
	\[
	|B_s|+\sum_{\nu=1}^r|C_s^\nu|\le C.
	\]
	For $1\le j\le n_*$,  we have 
\begin{align*}
	\,\mathrm d D_x^j\Phi_{t,s}(x)
	={}&\bigl[B_sD_x^j\Phi_{t,s}(x)+R_s^{(j)}\bigr]\,\mathrm d s\\
	&+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
	\bigl[C_s^\nu D_x^j\Phi_{t,s}(x)
	+S_s^{(j),\nu}\bigr]\,\mathrm d W_s^\nu,
\end{align*}
with
\[
D_x\Phi_{t,t}(x)=\mathrm{Id},
\qquad
D_x^j\Phi_{t,t}(x)=0\quad(j\ge2).
\]
Here, the remainders $R_s^{(j)}$ and $S_s^{(j),\nu}$ collect
the chain-rule terms involving only spatial derivatives of
the flow of orders below $j$.
Note that $R^{(1)}_s=S^{(1),\nu}_s=0$, and for $j\ge2$,
	\begin{equation}
		|R_s^{(j)}|+|S_s^{(j)}|
		\le C_j\sum_{\ell=2}^j
		\ \sum_{\substack{i_1+\cdots+i_\ell=j\\i_a\ge1}}
		\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}|D_x^{i_a}\Phi_{t,s}(x)|,
		\label{eq:flow-derivative-forcing}
	\end{equation}
	
For $j= 1$, \eqref{eq:flow-derivative-moment} is clearly true, we proceed by induction on $j$. 	Suppose the estimate holds for every order below $j$ and every
	finite exponent $q\ge2$. For each product in
	\eqref{eq:flow-derivative-forcing}, all $i_a<j$,  H\"older's
	inequality gives
	\begin{align*}
		&\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}\sup_{t\le s\le T}
		\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}|D_x^{i_a}\Phi_{t,s}(x)|^q\\
		&\quad\le
		\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}
		\left(
		\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}\sup_{t\le s\le T}
		|D_x^{i_a}\Phi_{t,s}(x)|^{q\ell}
		\right)^{1/\ell}
		\le C_{j,q}.
	\end{align*}
	Consequently,
	\[
	\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}\int_t^T
	\bigl(|R_s^{(j)}|^q+|S_s^{(j)}|^q\bigr)\,\mathrm d s
	\le C_{j,q}.
	\]
Then, BDG and Gronwall inequalities yield \eqref{eq:flow-derivative-moment}, which
completes the induction.
	
Now, we set
	\[
	\mathcal J_s:=D_x\Phi_{t,s}(x),
	\qquad
	\mathcal K_s:=\mathcal J_s^{-1}.
	\]
Then the	Matrix It\^o calculus yields
	\[
	\,\mathrm d\mathcal K_s
	=\mathcal K_s\left(-B_s+\sum_{\nu=1}^rC_s^\nu C_s^\nu\right)\,\mathrm d s
	-\sum_{\nu=1}^r\mathcal K_sC_s^\nu\,\mathrm d W_s^\nu,
	\qquad \mathcal K_t=\mathrm{Id}.
	\]
Since	the coefficients are uniformly bounded, we have
	\begin{equation}\label{x2}
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}
	\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}\sup_{t\le s\le T}|\mathcal K_s|^q
	\le C_q
	\qquad(q\ge2).
	\end{equation}
	For $j\ge2$, we have 
	\begin{align*}
		&\big|(D^j\Psi_{t,s})(\Phi_{t,s}(x))\big|\\
		&\quad\le C_j|\mathcal K_s|^j
		\sum_{\ell=1}^{j-1}
		\sum_{\substack{i_1+\cdots+i_\ell=j\\i_a\ge1}}
		\big|(D^\ell\Psi_{t,s})(\Phi_{t,s}(x))\big|
		\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}|D_x^{i_a}\Phi_{t,s}(x)|,
	\end{align*}
by induction which implies 
	\begin{equation}\label{x1}
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}
	\mathbb E^{\widetilde{\mathbb Q}}\sup_{t\le s\le T}
	\big|(D^j\Psi_{t,s})(\Phi_{t,s}(x))\big|^q
	\le C_{j,q},
	\qquad 1\le j\le n_*.
	\end{equation}
	
Note that, $J_{t,s}(x)=\det\mathcal J_s>0$ and
	$J_{t,s}(x)^{-1}=\det\mathcal K_s$. Then the Hadamard's inequality gives
	\[
	J_{t,s}(x)^q+J_{t,s}(x)^{-q}
	\le C_{d,q}\left(
	|\mathcal J_s|^{dq}+|\mathcal K_s|^{dq}
	\right).
	\]
Finally, combine \eqref{x2}, \eqref{x1} and \eqref{eq:flow-derivative-moment} prove
	\eqref{eq:maximal-inverse-flow-moments}.

label: eq:param-H-entropy-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
 \rho_j^{t,x}
 :=\inf\left\{s\in[0,T]:\int_0^s|H_a^{t,x}|^2\,\mathrm d a\ge j\right\}\wedge T.
\]
The exponential \eqref{eq:Ztx} stopped at $\rho_j^{t,x}$ is a true martingale.  Under the
probability $\widehat\mathbb Q_j^{t,x}$ on $\mathcal F_T$ with density
$Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}$, the process
\[
 Y_s-\int_0^{s\wedge\rho_j^{t,x}}H_a^{t,x}\,\mathrm d a,
 \qquad 0\le s\le T,
\]
is an Brownian motion independent of $W$.   Applying Lemma 
\ref{lem:flow-estimates}  gives
\[
 \sup_j\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q_j^{t,x}}
     \sup_{t\le s\le T}|X_s^{t,x}|^2
 \le C_k\left\langle x\right\rangle^2.
\]
Therefore, 
\begin{equation}
 \sup_j\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q_j^{t,x}}
     \int_0^{\rho_j^{t,x}}|H_s^{t,x}|^2\,\mathrm d s
 \le C_k\left\langle x\right\rangle^2.
 \label{eq:param-H-entropy-bound}
\end{equation}
Applying It\^o's formula to $\log Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}$, 
then, we have
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left[Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}
             \log Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}\right]
 =\frac12\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q_j^{t,x}}
      \int_0^{\rho_j^{t,x}}|H_s^{t,x}|^2\,\mathrm d s
 \le C_k\left\langle x\right\rangle^2.
 \label{eq:param-entropy}
\end{equation}

 By \eqref{eq:param-entropy}
and $r\log^+r\le r\log r+e^{-1}$, where
$\log^+r:=\max\{\log r,0\}$, for every $R>1$, and as $R\to\infty$, we have 
\[
\sup_j\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\!\left[Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}\mathbf 1_{\{Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}>R\}}\right]
\le \frac{1}{\log R}\sup_j\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}\log^+Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}]
\le \frac{C_k\left\langle x\right\rangle^2+e^{-1}}{\log R}
\longrightarrow0.
\]

Thus, $\{Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}\}_{j\ge1}$ is uniformly integrable, and $Z_{\rho_j^{t,x}}^{t,x}\to Z_T^{t,x}$ a.s., which implies that  $Z^{t,x}$ is a uniformly
integrable $\mathbb Q$-martingale on $[0,T]$.
Therefore,
\eqref{eq:Qhat-tx} defines an equivalent probability measure.
Note that, $Z_T^{t,x}=Z_\theta^{t,x}$ because $H^{t,x}=0$ after $\theta$. Then, 
Girsanov's theorem applied to $(W,Y)$  shows that
$W$ and $\widehat Y^{t,x}$ are independent $\mathbb F$-Brownian
motions under $\widehat\mathbb Q^{t,x}$. This completes the proof.

title: Remark
body_md:
The stopping factor $\chi^t$ in \eqref{eq:Htx} is crucial
	for the martingale argument under the present assumptions.
	Since $\theta\le\tau_k$,
	\[
	\int_0^T\chi_s^t|u_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\le k
	\qquad \mathbb Q\text{-a.s.}
	\]
	This bound remains valid under the localized equivalent
	measures and, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-estimates},
	yields \eqref{eq:param-H-entropy-bound} and the uniform
	entropy estimate \eqref{eq:param-entropy}.
	Without this stopping, almost sure finiteness of
	$\int_0^T|u_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s$ alone does not guarantee
	that the stochastic exponential is a true martingale.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:conditional-linear-BSDE}
Let $\widetilde\mathbb Q$ be a probability measure under which $B$ is an
$\mathbb F$-Brownian motion. For $q\ge2$ and the terminal condition $\eta$  satisfying  $\mathbb E^{\widetilde\mathbb Q}[|\eta|^q]<\infty$.  Suppose $(U,Z)$ is an
adapted solution of
\[
\,\mathrm d U_s=-R_s\,\mathrm d s+Z_s\,\mathrm d B_s,\qquad U_T=\eta,
\qquad t\le s\le T,
\]
satisfying
\[
\mathbb E^{\widetilde\mathbb Q}\left[
\sup_{t\le s\le T}|U_s|^q
+\left(\int_t^T|Z_s|^2\,\mathrm d s\right)^{q/2}
+\left(\int_t^T|R_s|\,\mathrm d s\right)^q
\right]<\infty.
\]
Then, for every stopping time $\rho$ with $t\le\rho\le T$,
\begin{align}
	|U_\rho|^q
	&+\mathbb E^{\widetilde\mathbb Q}\left[
	\left(\int_\rho^T|Z_s|^2\,\mathrm d s\right)^{q/2}
	\middle|\mathcal F_\rho\right] \notag\\
	&\le C_q\mathbb E^{\widetilde\mathbb Q}\left[
	|\eta|^q+\left(\int_\rho^T|R_s|\,\mathrm d s\right)^q
	\middle|\mathcal F_\rho\right].
	\label{eq:conditional-linear-BSDE}
\end{align}

title: Proof
body_md:
For fixed $N$, spatial differentiability through order $n_*$
in $\mathbb S^q\times\mathbb H^q\times\mathbb H^q$ follows
by applying standard stability estimates for Lipschitz BSDEs
successively to spatial difference quotients, using
\eqref{eq:hN-derivatives}, the regularity of $\gamma$,
and Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-estimates}.
We choose jointly measurable versions of the solutions
and their spatial derivatives.
	
Suppress  parameters  $(N,t,x)$.
	Differentiating \eqref{eq:truncated-BSDE} gives
	\begin{equation}
		\left\{
		\begin{aligned}
			\,\mathrm d D_x^\beta F_s
			&=-\left[H_s^\top D_x^\beta G_s+R_s^\beta\right]\,\mathrm d s
			+(D_x^\beta G_s)^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s
			+(D_x^\beta\widetilde G_s)^\top\,\mathrm d W_s,\\
			D_x^\beta F_T&=D_x^\beta\Gamma,
		\end{aligned}
		\right.
		\label{eq:derivative-BSDE}
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{equation}
		R_s^\beta
		:=\sum_{0<\eta\le\beta}\binom{\beta}{\eta}
		(D_x^\eta H_s)^\top D_x^{\beta-\eta}G_s,
		\qquad R_s^0:=0.
		\label{eq:R-beta}
	\end{equation}
	Here, $0<\eta\le\beta$ means that $\eta$ is a nonzero multi-index
	with $0\le\eta_k\le\beta_k$ for every $k=1,\ldots,d$, and
	$\displaystyle \binom{\beta}{\eta}
	:=\prod_{k=1}^d\binom{\beta_k}{\eta_k}
	=\prod_{k=1}^d\frac{\beta_k!}{\eta_k!(\beta_k-\eta_k)!}$
	is the multi-index binomial coefficient.
	
	Write
	\[
	\widehat\mathbb Q:=\widehat\mathbb Q^{N,t,x}, \qquad 
	\widehat\mathbb E_\rho[\cdot]
	:=\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q}[\cdot\mid\mathcal F_\rho], 	
	\qquad
	\mathfrak D_j(\rho)
	:=1+\sum_{i=1}^j|D_x^iX_\rho^{t,x}|.
	\]
	Under $\widehat\mathbb Q$,    \eqref{eq:derivative-BSDE} becomes:
	\begin{equation}
		\,\mathrm d D_x^\beta F_s
		=-R_s^{\beta}\,\mathrm d s
		+(D_x^\beta G_s)^\top\,\mathrm d\widehat Y_s^{N,t,x}
		+(D_x^\beta\widetilde G_s)^\top\,\mathrm d W_s.
		\label{eq:derivative-under-Qhat}
	\end{equation}
	
	
	We prove by induction on $j$, that for every
	$2\le q<\infty$,  $|\beta|\le j$ and $t\le\rho\le T$, the following holds:
	\begin{equation}
		\begin{aligned}
			|D_x^\beta F_\rho|^q
			&+\widehat\mathbb E_\rho\left[
			\left(\int_\rho^T
			\bigl(|D_x^\beta G_s|^2
			+|D_x^\beta\widetilde G_s|^2\bigr)\,\mathrm d s
			\right)^{q/2}\right]\\
			&\le P_{j,q}\bigl(\mathfrak D_j(\rho)\bigr).
		\end{aligned}
		\label{eq:closed-conditional-induction}
	\end{equation}

	
Indeed, 	for $j=0$, \eqref{eq:FN-representation} and
	Lemma~\ref{lem:conditional-linear-BSDE} give
	\eqref{eq:closed-conditional-induction} with a constant polynomial.
	Suppose the estimate holds through order $j-1$ at every finite
	exponent, and let $|\beta|=j$.
	Since $\Gamma=\gamma(X_T^{t,x})$, the chain rule and
	Lemma~\ref{lem:conditional-flow-polynomial} give
	\[
	\widehat\mathbb E_\rho\left[
	|D_x^\beta\Gamma|^q
	+\sum_{0<\eta\le\beta}
	\left(\int_\rho^T|D_x^\eta H_s|^2\,\mathrm d s\right)^q
	\right]
	\le P_{j,q}\bigl(\mathfrak D_j(\rho)\bigr).
	\]
	Moreover, conditional Cauchy--Schwarz yields
	\begin{equation}\label{xx1}
	\begin{aligned}
		&\widehat\mathbb E_\rho
		\left(\int_\rho^T|R_s^\beta|\,\mathrm d s\right)^q\\
		&\quad\le C_{\beta,q}
		\sum_{0<\eta\le\beta}
		\left\{
		\widehat\mathbb E_\rho
		\left(\int_\rho^T|D_x^\eta H_s|^2\,\mathrm d s\right)^q
		\right\}^{1/2}
		\left\{
		\widehat\mathbb E_\rho
		\left(\int_\rho^T|D_x^{\beta-\eta}G_s|^2\,\mathrm d s\right)^q
		\right\}^{1/2}\\
		&\quad\le P_{j,q}\bigl(\mathfrak D_j(\rho)\bigr),
	\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
	where the last inequality uses the induction hypothesis at
	exponent $2q$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:conditional-linear-BSDE} to
	\eqref{eq:derivative-under-Qhat} then closes the induction.
	
Applying \eqref{eq:closed-conditional-induction} at times in a
countable dense subset of $[t,T]$, and using path continuity
together with the equivalence of $\widehat{\mathbb Q}$ and $\mathbb Q$, we obtain
	\[
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}|D_x^\beta F_s|^q
	\le
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}
	P_{|\beta|,q}\bigl(\mathfrak D_{|\beta|}(s)\bigr),
	\qquad \mathbb Q\text{-a.s.}
	\]
Note that,  for some finite
	integer $M$, we have 
	\[
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}
	P_{|\beta|,q}\bigl(\mathfrak D_{|\beta|}(s)\bigr)
	\le
	C_{\beta,q}\left(
	1+\sum_{i=1}^{|\beta|}
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}|D_x^iX_s^{t,x}|^M
	\right).
	\]
	Taking $\mathbb Q$-expectations and applying
	Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-estimates} at exponent $M$ proves
	\eqref{eq:uniform-F-parameter}.
	
	
Applying Lemma \ref{lem:flow-estimates}, we obtain,  for  	$ 0<|\eta|\le n_*$, 
	$1\le p<\infty$ and $0<|\eta|\le n_*$,
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(1+\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^p
	\le C_{k,p}\left\langle x\right\rangle^{2p},
	\qquad
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(\int_t^T|D_x^\eta H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^p
	\le C_{k,\eta,p}.
	\]
The simple calculations for 
\eqref{eq:derivative-BSDE} gives the following energy
estimate: 
	\begin{align*}
		&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(\int_t^T
		\bigl(|D_x^\beta G_s|^2
		+|D_x^\beta\widetilde G_s|^2\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s
		\right)^{q/2}\\
		&\quad\le C_q\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left[
		\sup_{t\le s\le T}|D_x^\beta F_s|^q
		\left(1+\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^{q/2}
		+\left(\int_t^T|R_s^\beta|\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^q
		\right].
	\end{align*}
	By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and
	\eqref{eq:uniform-F-parameter} at exponent $2q$,
	\begin{equation}\label{001}
		\begin{aligned}
			&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left[
			\sup_{t\le s\le T}|D_x^\beta F_s|^q
			\left(1+\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^{q/2}
			\right]\\
			&\quad\le
			\left(\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{t\le s\le T}
			|D_x^\beta F_s|^{2q}\right)^{1/2}
			\left[
			\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(1+\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^q
			\right]^{1/2}\\
			&\quad\le C_{k,\beta,q}\left\langle x\right\rangle^q.
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
	
	We now prove \eqref{eq:uniform-G-parameter} by induction on
	$|\beta|$, simultaneously for all finite exponents $q\ge2$.
	For $\beta=0$, we have $R^0=0$, so the preceding energy
	estimate and \eqref{001} give
	\eqref{eq:uniform-G-parameter} at every such exponent.
	
	Suppose that \eqref{eq:uniform-G-parameter} holds for all
	derivatives of order at most $j-1$ and every finite exponent
	at least $2$, and let $|\beta|=j$.
	Using \eqref{eq:R-beta}, we obtain
	\begin{equation}\label{00}
		\begin{aligned}
			&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(\int_t^T|R_s^\beta|\,\mathrm{d}s\right)^q\\
			&\quad\le C_{\beta,q}
			\sum_{0<\eta\le\beta}
			\left\{
			\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(
			\int_t^T|D_x^\eta H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
			\right)^q
			\right\}^{1/2}
			\left\{
			\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(
			\int_t^T|D_x^{\beta-\eta}G_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
			\right)^q
			\right\}^{1/2}\\
			&\quad\le C_{k,\beta,q}\left\langle x\right\rangle^q.
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
	Substituting \eqref{001} and \eqref{00} into the energy
	estimate proves \eqref{eq:uniform-G-parameter} for
	$|\beta|=j$ and closes the induction.
	All constants are independent of $N,t,x$.

label: lem:localized-martingale-stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:localized-martingale-stability}

Fix $a\in[0,T]$, and let $B$ be an $\mathbb F$-Brownian motion.
Assume that $\zeta_j\to\zeta$ in $L^1$ and that the martingales
\[
M_s^j=\mathbb E[\zeta_j\mid\mathcal F_s],
\qquad
M_s=\mathbb E[\zeta\mid\mathcal F_s],
\qquad a\le s\le T,
\]
admit the representations
\[
M_s^j=M_a^j+\int_a^s K_r^j\,\mathrm{d}B_r,
\qquad
M_s=M_a+\int_a^s K_r\,\mathrm{d}B_r.
\]
For fixed $L >0$, define 
\[
 \kappa_L^j:=\inf\{s\in[a,T]:|M_s^j|+|M_s|>L\}\wedge T,
\]
one has
\begin{align}
 \lim_{L\to\infty}\sup_j\mathbb P(\kappa_L^j<T)&=0,
 \label{eq:martingale-stability-localization-prob}\\
 \mathbb E\int_a^{\kappa_L^j}|K_s^j-K_s|^2\,\mathrm d s&\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:martingale-stability-local-H2}
\end{align}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The Doob's weak $L^1$
inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
	\mathbb P\left(
	\sup_{a\le s\le T}|M_s^j-M_s|>\varepsilon
	\right)
	&\le
	\varepsilon^{-1}\mathbb E|\zeta_j-\zeta|
	\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Note that,
\[
\mathbb P(\kappa_L^j<T)
\le
\frac{2}{L}
\left(\mathbb E|\zeta_j|+\mathbb E|\zeta|\right).
\]
Since $\zeta_j\to\zeta$ in $L^1$, and 
$\sup_j\mathbb E|\zeta_j|<\infty$. Hence
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\sup_j\mathbb P(\kappa_L^j<T)=0.
\]

Let $D^j:=M^j-M$ and
$E_L^j:=\{|M_a^j|+|M_a|\le L\}\in\mathcal F_a$.  Since
$\kappa_L^j=a$ on $(E_L^j)^c$ and
$|D_{\kappa_L^j}^j-D_a^j|\le2L$ on $E_L^j$, we have 
\[
 \mathbb E\int_a^{\kappa_L^j}|K_s^j-K_s|^2\,\mathrm d s
 =\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbf 1_{E_L^j}
 |D_{\kappa_L^j}^j-D_a^j|^2\right]\longrightarrow0.
\]
This completes the proof.

label: prop:density-stability
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Density-martingale stability

title: Proof
body_md:
We fix $(t,x)$ and suppress these indices. We first prove existence
	and uniqueness for \eqref{eq:untruncated-BSDE}, and then establish
	the asserted convergence.
	
	By \eqref{eq:Ztx} and Proposition~\ref{prop:param-likelihood},
	$Z$ is a strictly positive uniformly integrable $\mathbb Q$-martingale.
	For $t\le s\le T$, define
	\[
	M_s:=\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[Z_T\Gamma\mid\mathcal F_s].
	\]
This is a continuous uniformly integrable martingale. Therefore, there exists predictable locally
square-integrable processes $K^Y$ and $K^W$ such that 
	\[
	M_s=M_t+\int_t^s(K_a^Y)^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_a
	+\int_t^s(K_a^W)^\top\,\mathrm{d}W_a.
	\]
	Set
	\[
	F_s:=\frac{M_s}{Z_s}
	=\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q}[\Gamma\mid\mathcal F_s],
	\]
	and define
	\begin{equation}
		G_s:=\frac{K_s^Y}{Z_s}-F_sH_s,
		\qquad
		\widetilde G_s:=\frac{K_s^W}{Z_s}.
		\label{eq:limit-integrands-definition}
	\end{equation}
Then,  processes in
\eqref{eq:limit-integrands-definition} are locally square-integrable, and  
	\begin{equation}
		|F_s|\le\|\gamma\|_\infty,
		\qquad t\le s\le T.
		\label{eq:limit-F-bound}
	\end{equation}
	Since $\mathrm{d}Z_s=Z_sH_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s$,
	It\^o's formula gives
	\[
	\mathrm{d}F_s
	=-H_s^\top G_s\,\mathrm{d}s
	+G_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s
	+\widetilde G_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}W_s,
	\qquad F_T=\Gamma.
	\]
	
	We next verify square integrability under $\mathbb Q$.
	The growth assumption, $\theta\le\tau_k$, and
	Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-estimates} imply
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		\le C\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T
		\chi_s^t\bigl(1+|X_s^{t,x}|^2+|u_s|^2\bigr)
		\,\mathrm{d}s
		\le C_k\left\langle x\right\rangle^2.
		\label{eq:H-square-integrable}
	\end{equation}
	Let
	\[
	\eta_j:=\inf\left\{s\in[t,T]:
	\int_t^s
	\bigl(|G_a|^2+|\widetilde G_a|^2+|H_a|^2\bigr)
	\,\mathrm{d}a\ge j\right\}\wedge T.
	\]
	Then $\eta_j\uparrow T$ almost surely.
	Applying It\^o's formula to $|F|^2$ on $[t,\eta_j]$
	and taking expectations, we obtain
	\begin{align*}
		&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^{\eta_j}
		\bigl(|G_s|^2+|\widetilde G_s|^2\bigr)
		\,\mathrm{d}s\\
		&\quad=
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q|F_{\eta_j}|^2-\mathbb E^\mathbb Q|F_t|^2
		+2\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^{\eta_j}
		F_sH_s^\top G_s\,\mathrm{d}s\\
		&\quad\le
		\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		+\frac12\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^{\eta_j}|G_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		+2\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s.
	\end{align*}
Consequently, 
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T
		\bigl(|G_s|^2+|\widetilde G_s|^2\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s
		\le 2\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		+4\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		<\infty.
		\label{eq:limit-integrands-H2}
	\end{equation}
	Thus $(F,G,\widetilde G)$ is a solution in the class stated in the
	proposition. 
	
	To prove uniqueness, let
	$(F^i,G^i,\widetilde G^i)$, $i=1,2$, be two solutions
	in this class, and use bars for their differences.
	Under $\widehat\mathbb Q$, Proposition~\ref{prop:param-likelihood}
	transforms the difference equation into
	\[
	\mathrm{d}\bar F_s
	=\bar G_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}\widehat Y_s^{t,x}
	+\overline{\widetilde G}_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}W_s,
	\qquad \bar F_T=0.
	\]
	Since $\bar F$ is bounded, it is a true
	$\widehat\mathbb Q$-martingale. Hence
	\[
	\bar F_s=\mathbb E^{\widehat\mathbb Q}[\bar F_T\mid\mathcal F_s]=0,
	\qquad t\le s\le T.
	\]
	Its quadratic variation gives
	\[
	\int_t^T
	\bigl(|\bar G_s|^2+|\overline{\widetilde G}_s|^2\bigr)
	\,\mathrm{d}s=0,
	\qquad \widehat\mathbb Q\text{-a.s.},
	\]
	and therefore also $\mathbb Q$-almost surely.
	This proves uniqueness.
	
	We now establish convergence of the truncated solutions.
	By \eqref{eq:hN-pointwise}, \eqref{eq:hN-dominated},
	\eqref{eq:H-square-integrable},  we have 
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_s^N-H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		\longrightarrow0.
		\label{eq:H-strong}
	\end{equation}
The BDG 	and  Cauchy-Schwarz  inequalities give
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{t\le s\le T}
	\left|\int_t^s(H_a^N-H_a)^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_a\right|^2
	\le4\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_a^N-H_a|^2\,\mathrm{d}a
	\longrightarrow0, 
	\]
and 
	\begin{align*}
		&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T
		\bigl||H_a^N|^2-|H_a|^2\bigr|\,\mathrm{d}a\\
		&\quad\le
		\left(\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T|H_a^N-H_a|^2\,\mathrm{d}a\right)^{1/2}
		\left(\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^T
		(|H_a^N|+|H_a|)^2\,\mathrm{d}a\right)^{1/2}
		\longrightarrow0.
	\end{align*}
	Therefore,
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q	&\sup_{0\le s\le T}
		|\log Z_s^N-\log Z_s|
		\longrightarrow0,
	\end{align*}
	which implies
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{0\le s\le T}|Z_s^N-Z_s|
		\longrightarrow0
		\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
		\label{eq:Z-uniform-probability}
	\end{equation}

	The entropy estimates \eqref{eq:ZN-entropy} and
	\eqref{eq:param-entropy}, together with
	$r\log^+r\le r\log r+e^{-1}$, imply
	\[
	\sup_N\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[Z_T^N\log^+Z_T^N]
	+\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[Z_T\log^+Z_T]<\infty.
	\]
	Thus de la Vall\'ee--Poussin's criterion and
	\eqref{eq:Z-uniform-probability} yield
	\begin{equation}
		Z_T^N\longrightarrow Z_T
		\qquad\text{in }L^1(\mathbb Q).
		\label{eq:Z-L1}
	\end{equation}
	
	For $t\le s\le T$, define
	\[
	M_s^N:=\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[Z_T^N\Gamma\mid\mathcal F_s].
	\]
	By Bayes' formula,
	\[
	F_s^N=\frac{M_s^N}{Z_s^N},
	\qquad
	|F_s^N|\vee|F_s|\le\|\gamma\|_\infty.
	\]
	By \eqref{eq:Z-L1}, we have 
	\[
	\|Z_T^N\Gamma-Z_T\Gamma\|_{L^1(\mathbb Q)}
	\le\|\gamma\|_\infty\|Z_T^N-Z_T\|_{L^1(\mathbb Q)}
	\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	Hence,  for every
	$\varepsilon>0$,
	\[
	\mathbb Q\left(
	\sup_{t\le s\le T}|M_s^N-M_s|>\varepsilon
	\right)
	\le\frac1\varepsilon
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q|(Z_T^N-Z_T)\Gamma|
	\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	Thus
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{t\le s\le T}|M_s^N-M_s|
		\longrightarrow0
		\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
		\label{eq:M-uniform-probability}
	\end{equation}
	
	Define, 
	$\underline Z:=\inf_{t\le s\le T}Z_s>0$. It follows that 
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{t\le s\le T}|F_s^N-F_s|
		\longrightarrow0
		\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
		\label{eq:F-uniform-probability}
	\end{equation}
	For every $\eta>0$,
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{t\le s\le T}|F_s^N-F_s|^2
		&\le \eta^2
		+4\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		\mathbb Q\left(
		\sup_{t\le s\le T}|F_s^N-F_s|>\eta
		\right).
	\end{align*}
	Letting first $N\to\infty$ and then $\eta\downarrow0$
	proves \eqref{eq:F-strong}.
	
	We next prove convergence of the martingale integrands.
	Write
	\[
	\mathrm{d}M_s^N
	=(K_s^{N,Y})^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s
	+(K_s^{N,W})^\top\,\mathrm{d}W_s.
	\]
	It\^o's formula applied to $M^N=Z^NF^N$ gives
	\begin{equation}
		K^{N,Y}=Z^N(G^N+F^NH^N),
		\qquad K^{N,W}=Z^N\widetilde G^N.
	\end{equation}
	Similarly,
	\begin{equation}
		K^Y=Z(G+FH),
		\qquad K^W=Z\widetilde G.
		\label{eq:K-identity}
	\end{equation}
	
	Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:localized-martingale-stability}
	with $a=t$, $B=(Y,W)$,
	$\zeta_N=Z_T^N\Gamma$, and $\zeta=Z_T\Gamma$,
	and denote the resulting stopping times by $\kappa_L^N$.
	Define
	\begin{align*}
		A_s^N&:=Z_s^N+Z_s+(Z_s^N)^{-1}+Z_s^{-1},\\
		B_s^N&:=\int_t^s
		(|H_a^N|^2+|H_a|^2)\,\mathrm{d}a,\\
		\rho_L^N&:=\inf\{s\in[t,T]:
		A_s^N\vee B_s^N\ge L\}\wedge T,
		\qquad
		\sigma_L^N:=\kappa_L^N\wedge\rho_L^N.
	\end{align*}
Since $Z$ is strictly positive and continuous,
\eqref{eq:Z-uniform-probability} also gives
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{0\le s\le T}|(Z_s^N)^{-1}-Z_s^{-1}|
		\longrightarrow0
		\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
		\label{11}
	\end{equation}
	Lemma~\ref{lem:localized-martingale-stability},
	\eqref{eq:H-strong}, \eqref{eq:Z-uniform-probability},
	and \eqref{11} yield
	\begin{align}
		\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
		\mathbb Q(\sigma_L^N<T)&=0,
		\label{eq:common-localization-prob}\\
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^{\sigma_L^N}
		\left(
		|K_s^{N,Y}-K_s^Y|^2
		+|K_s^{N,W}-K_s^W|^2
		\right)\,\mathrm{d}s
		&\longrightarrow0,
		\label{eq:K-local-H2}
	\end{align}
	where the second convergence holds for every fixed $L$.
	
On $[t,\sigma_L^N]$, we have 
	\begin{align*}
		G^N-G
		&=\frac{K^{N,Y}-K^Y}{Z^N}
		+K^Y\left(\frac1{Z^N}-\frac1Z\right)
		-(F^NH^N-FH),\\
		\widetilde G^N-\widetilde G
		&=\frac{K^{N,W}-K^W}{Z^N}
		+K^W\left(\frac1{Z^N}-\frac1Z\right).
	\end{align*}
	Moreover,
	\begin{align*}
		&\int_t^{\sigma_L^N}
		|F_s^NH_s^N-F_sH_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s\\
		&\quad\le
		2L\sup_{t\le s\le T}|F_s^N-F_s|^2
		+2\|\gamma\|_\infty^2
		\int_t^T|H_s^N-H_s|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		\longrightarrow0
		\quad\text{in  $\mathbb Q$-probability},
	\end{align*}
and 
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_t^{\sigma_L^N}
	(|K_s^Y|^2+|K_s^W|^2)\,\mathrm{d}s
	=\mathbb E^\mathbb Q|M_{\sigma_L^N}-M_t|^2
	\le4L^2.
	\]
	Thus \eqref{eq:K-local-H2}, \eqref{11}, and the preceding
	estimates imply
	\begin{equation}
		\int_t^{\sigma_L^N}
		\bigl(
		|G_s^N-G_s|^2
		+|\widetilde G_s^N-\widetilde G_s|^2
		\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s
		\longrightarrow0
		\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
		\label{eq:G-local-prob}
	\end{equation}
	Combining \eqref{eq:G-local-prob} with
	\eqref{eq:common-localization-prob}, we obtain
	\[
	\int_t^T
	\bigl(
	|G_s^N-G_s|^2
	+|\widetilde G_s^N-\widetilde G_s|^2
	\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s
	\longrightarrow0
	\qquad\text{in $\mathbb Q$-probability}.
	\]
	
	For any fixed $q>2$, Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-parameter}
	and \eqref{eq:limit-integrands-H2} give
	\begin{align*}
		&\sup_N\mathbb E^\mathbb Q
		\left(
		\int_t^T(|G_s^N|^2+|\widetilde G_s^N|^2)\,\mathrm{d}s
		\right)^{q/2}\\
		&\qquad+
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q
		\left(
		\int_t^T(|G_s|^2+|\widetilde G_s|^2)\,\mathrm{d}s
		\right)^{q/2}
		<\infty.
	\end{align*}
	Consequently, the random variables
	\[
	\int_t^T
	\bigl(
	|G_s^N-G_s|^2
	+|\widetilde G_s^N-\widetilde G_s|^2
	\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}s
	\]
	are uniformly integrable. Vitali's theorem proves
	\eqref{eq:G-strong}.
	
	Finally, take $t=0$. For each fixed $x$,
	\eqref{eq:F-strong}--\eqref{eq:G-strong} give
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{0\le s\le T}
	|F_s^{N,0,x}-F_s^{0,x}|^2\longrightarrow0,
	\qquad
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^T
	|G_s^{N,0,x}-G_s^{0,x}|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
	\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	For each $N$, these expected errors are measurable functions
	of $x$.
	The dominated convergence theorem  proves
	\eqref{eq:local-parameter-F0}--\eqref{eq:local-parameter-G0}.
	
	For each fixed $R<\infty$, the local convergences imply that
	$(F^{N,0,\cdot})_N$ and $(G^{N,0,\cdot})_N$ are Cauchy in
	\[
	L^2\bigl(B_R\times\Omega;C([0,T])\bigr)
	\quad\text{and}\quad
	L^2\bigl(B_R\times\Omega\times[0,T];\mathbb R^m\bigr),
	\]
	respectively. Completeness yields jointly measurable local
	limits, which agree almost everywhere on overlaps by uniqueness
	of limits. Taking $R=1,2,\ldots$ and patching these local limits
	gives jointly measurable representatives of $F^{0,\cdot}$ and
	$G^{0,\cdot}$ on $\Omega\times[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$.

body_md:
\label{lem:reference-stopping-functional}
	Let 
	$
	\mathcal G_t^k:=\mathcal F^Y_{t\wedge\tau_k},
	\mathbb G^k=(\mathcal G_t^k)_{0\le t\le T}.
	$
	The filtration $\mathbb G^k$ has predictable representation with respect to
	$Y_{\cdot\wedge\tau_k}$. If $\theta\le\tau_k$ is an
	$\mathbb F^Y$-stopping time, it is also a $\mathbb G^k$-stopping time, and
	\begin{equation}
		\mathcal G_{t\wedge\theta}^k=\mathcal F^Y_{t\wedge\theta},
		\qquad \mathcal G_\theta^k=\mathcal F^Y_\theta.
		\label{eq:filtrations-agree-through-theta}
	\end{equation}
	Moreover, every $\mathbb G^k$-local martingale, viewed in $\mathbb F$, is a local
	martingale strongly orthogonal to $W$.
head: environment
name: Stopped reference observation filtration

title: Proof
body_md:
The predictable representation property is preserved under stopping; see
\citet[Chapter~III, Section~4]{JacodShiryaev2003}.  Indeed, for
$\xi\in L^2(\mathcal F^Y_{\tau_k})$ and let 
$M_t :=\mathbb E^\mathbb Q[\xi\mid\mathcal F_t^Y]=M_0+\int_0^tZ_s^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s$, we have 
\[
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q[\xi\mid\mathcal G_t^k]
 =M_{t\wedge\tau_k}
 =M_0+\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_k}Z_s^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s.
\]
Note that 
\eqref{eq:filtrations-agree-through-theta} is clearly true.  Finally, every
$\mathbb G^k$-local martingale $N_t$ has the form
$N_0+\int_0^{\cdot\wedge\tau_k}Z_s^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s$ after localization, and hence
\[
 \left[\int_0^{\cdot\wedge\tau_k}Z_s^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s,W^\nu\right]_t=0,
 \qquad 1\le\nu\le r.
\]

name: Weighted stochastic-flow multiplier

title: Proof
body_md:
Let  $V_m(x)=\left\langle x\right\rangle^{-m}$, direct differentiation gives
\begin{align*}
 |DV_m(x)|\le C_mV_m(x)\left\langle x\right\rangle^{-1}, \qquad
 |D^2V_m(x)|\le C_mV_m(x)\left\langle x\right\rangle^{-2},
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
	\bigl|b(x,v)^\top DV_m(x)\bigr|
	+\left|\sum_{i,j=1}^d
	a^{ij}(x,v)D_{ij}V_m(x)\right|
	&\le C_m(1+|v|^2)V_m(x),\\
	\bigl|DV_m(x)\sigma(x,v)\bigr|^2
	&\le C_m(1+|v|^2)V_m(x)^2.
\end{align*}

Set $V_s=V_m(\Phi_s(y))$.  By It\^o's formula,
\[
\,\mathrm d V_s=V_s\mu_s\,\mathrm d s+V_s\nu_s^\top\,\mathrm d W_s,
\]
where
\begin{align*}
	\mu_s
	&:=
	\frac{\chi_s^0}{V_m(\Phi_s(y))}
	\left[
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	b^i(\Phi_s(y),u_s)D_iV_m(\Phi_s(y))
	+\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^d
	a^{ij}(\Phi_s(y),u_s)D_{ij}V_m(\Phi_s(y))
	\right],\\
	\nu_s^\ell
	&:=
	\frac{\chi_s^0}{V_m(\Phi_s(y))}
	\sum_{i=1}^d
	D_iV_m(\Phi_s(y))
	\sigma^{i\ell}(\Phi_s(y),u_s),
	\qquad \ell=1,\ldots,r.
\end{align*}
It follows that
\[
\int_0^T\bigl(|\mu_s|+|\nu_s|^2\bigr)\,\mathrm d s
\le C_m\int_0^\theta(1+|u_s|^2)\,\mathrm d s
\le C_m(T+k).
\]


Therefore, for every finite $q\ge1$, we have 
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{s\le\theta}V_m(\Phi_s(y))^q
 \le C_{m,q,k}V_m(y)^q.
 \label{eq:negative-flow-moment}
\end{equation}

All finite moments of
$\sup_{s\le\theta}|J_s(y)P_s(y)|$ are bounded uniformly in $y$ by
\eqref{eq:flow-derivative-moment} and \eqref{eq:maximal-inverse-flow-moments}.  Hence, H\"older's inequality and
\eqref{eq:negative-flow-moment} give
\[
 \left\|\sup_{s\le\theta}
 \left\langle \Phi_s(y)\right\rangle^{-m}J_s(y)|P_s(y)|\right\|_{L^q}
 \le C_{m,q,k,P}\left\langle y\right\rangle^{-m}.
\]

	$\mathbb K^s=(\mathcal K_r^s)_{r\in[s,T]}$ by

		$
		\mathcal F_r^Y\subset\mathcal K_r^s.

		\item[(ii)]
		The random time $\rho_s:=s\vee\theta$ is a
		$\mathbb K^s$-stopping time, and
		$
		\mathcal F_\theta^Y\subset\mathcal K_{\rho_s}^s.

title: Proof

Note that
\[
 \mathcal F_r^Y
 \subset \mathcal F_s^Y\vee\sigma(Y_a-Y_s:s\le a\le r)
 \subset\mathcal K_r^s.
\]
Let $A\in\mathcal F_\theta^Y$, for every $r\in[s,T]$,
\[
A\cap\{\rho_s\le r\}
=A\cap\{\theta\le r\}
\in\mathcal F_r^Y
\subset\mathcal K_r^s.
\]
Hence, 
$A\in\mathcal K_{\rho_s}^s$, and 
$
\mathcal F_\theta^Y\subset\mathcal K_{\rho_s}^s.
$

title: Proof
body_md:
For $q>d$, Proposition \ref{prop:uniform-parameter} and the
	Banach-valued Kolmogorov continuity criterion yield a version such that
	$
	x\longmapsto \bigl(F_r^{N,0,x}\bigr)_{0\le r\le T}
	$ 
	is  continuous as a $C([0,T])$-valued map. Since
	$(s,x)\mapsto\Psi_s(x)$ is jointly continuous, the identity
	\[
	f_s^N(x)=F_s^{N,0,\Psi_s(x)},
	\qquad (s,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d,
	\]
	then yields a version of
	$\bigl(f_s^N(x)\bigr)_{(s,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d}$
	that is  continuous in $(s,x)$.


Fix $s,x$.  Let
$X^{s,x}_{\cdot}$ be the unique $\mathbb K^s$-adapted solution of
\eqref{eq:forward-flow} with $t=s$. 
Then, the BSDE \eqref{eq:truncated-BSDE} with
$(t,x)=(s,x)$ and terminal value $\Gamma^{s,x} =\gamma(X_\theta^{s,x})$ admits a unique
solution $
\left(F^{N,s,x},\,G^{N,s,x},\,\widetilde{G}^{N,s,x}\right)
$ in the filtration $\mathbb K^s$. Consequenly,  $F^{N,s,x}_s$
is $\mathcal F_s^Y$
measurable. 

 Uniqueness in the full filtration and \eqref{eq:decoupling-N}
give
\[
 \mathbf 1_{\{s\le\theta\}}f_s^N(x)
 =\mathbf 1_{\{s\le\theta\}}F_s^{N,s,x},
 \qquad
 \mathbf 1_{\{s>\theta\}}f_\theta^N(x)
 =\mathbf 1_{\{s>\theta\}}\gamma(x),
\]
which is \eqref{eq:diagonal-Y}. 

For each fixed $s$, applying the above identity at rational
spatial points and using spatial continuity shows that
$f_{s\wedge\theta}^N$ is an $\mathcal F_s^Y$-measurable
$C(\mathbb R^d)$-valued random variable.
Thus $f^N_{\cdot\wedge\theta}$ is an $\mathbb F^Y$-adapted
continuous process.
By \eqref{eq:filtrations-agree-through-theta},
\[
\mathcal F_{s\wedge\theta}^Y
=\mathcal G_{s\wedge\theta}^k
\subset\mathcal G_s^k.
\]
Hence $f^N_{\cdot\wedge\theta}$ is $\mathbb G^k$-adapted.

body_md:
\label{lem:flow-composition}
	
	\textnormal{(i) Inverse-flow dynamics.}
	For every component $\ell$, the inverse flow satisfies
	\begin{equation}
		\mathrm{d}\Psi_s^\ell(x)
		=\beta_s^\ell(x)\,\mathrm{d}s
		+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(x)\,\mathrm{d}W_s^\nu,
		\label{eq:inverse-flow-SDE}
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{align}
		\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(x)
		&=-D_i\Psi_s^\ell(x)\sigma_s^{i\nu}(x),
		\label{eq:inverse-flow-diffusion}\\
		\beta_s^\ell(x)
		&=-D_i\Psi_s^\ell(x)b_s^i(x)
		+\frac12a_s^{ip}(x)D_{ip}\Psi_s^\ell(x)
		\notag\\
		&\quad
		+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		D_i\Psi_s^\ell(x)
		D_p\sigma_s^{i\nu}(x)\sigma_s^{p\nu}(x).
		\label{eq:inverse-flow-drift}
	\end{align}
	
	\textnormal{(ii) Inverse-flow composition.}
		Suppose that $(U,A,B,C)$ satisfies condition
	$\mathrm{(IW)}_{n_*}$.
	Then,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathrm{d}U_s(\Psi_s(x))
		=\widehat A_s\,\mathrm{d}s
		+\widehat B_s^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s
		+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		\widehat C_s^\nu\,\mathrm{d}W_s^\nu,
		\label{eq:inverse-pullback-formula}
	\end{equation}
	where
	\begin{align}
		\widehat A_s(x)
		={}&A_s(\Psi_s(x))
		+D_\ell U_s(\Psi_s(x))\beta_s^\ell(x)
		\notag\\
		&+\frac12D_{\ell q}U_s(\Psi_s(x))
		\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(x)\zeta_s^{q\nu}(x)
		\notag\\
		&+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		D_\ell C_s^\nu(\Psi_s(x))
		\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(x),
		\label{eq:inverse-pullback-drift}\\
		\widehat B_s(x)
		={}&B_s(\Psi_s(x)),
		\label{eq:inverse-pullback-Y}\\
		\widehat C_s^\nu(x)
		={}&C_s^\nu(\Psi_s(x))
		-D_i\bigl[U_s(\Psi_s(x))\bigr]\sigma_s^{i\nu}(x).
		\label{eq:inverse-pullback-W}
	\end{align}
	


	
	\textnormal{(iii) Forward-flow composition.}
	Suppose that $(v,A,B,C)$ satisfies condition
	$\mathrm{(IW)}_{n_*}$. Then, 
	\begin{align}
		\mathrm{d}v_s(X_s^{t,x})
		={}&
		\left[
		A_s+L_sv_s
		+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		D_iC_s^\nu\,\sigma_s^{i\nu}
		\right](X_s^{t,x})\,\mathrm{d}s
		+B_s(X_s^{t,x})^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s
		\notag\\
		&+\sum_{\nu=1}^r
		\left[
		C_s^\nu+D_iv_s\,\sigma_s^{i\nu}
		\right](X_s^{t,x})\,\mathrm{d}W_s^\nu.
		\label{eq:forward-flow-IW}
	\end{align}
	

	
	For every $R<\infty$, there exists an event
	$\Omega_R^{\mathrm{inv}}$ with
	$\mathbb Q(\Omega_R^{\mathrm{inv}})=1$ such that, on
	$\Omega_R^{\mathrm{inv}}$, the integral identity obtained from
	\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-formula} by pairing with any
	$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B_R)$ holds for every $s\in[0,\theta]$.
	
	For every fixed deterministic $t$ and every $R<\infty$, there exists
	an event $\Omega_{t,R}^{\mathrm{for}}$ with
	$\mathbb Q(\Omega_{t,R}^{\mathrm{for}})=1$, independent of the starting
	point $x$, such that the integral form of
	\eqref{eq:forward-flow-IW} holds on
	$\Omega_{t,R}^{\mathrm{for}}$ for every $s\in[t,\theta]$ and
	Lebesgue-a.e.\ $x\in B_R$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The coefficients of the inverse-flow dynamics are obtained by
applying the It\^o--Wentzell formula to the identity
$\Psi_s(\Phi_s(y))=y$; see \citet[Section~4.6]{Kunita1990}.
This gives 
\begin{align*}
 \zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(\Phi_s)
 +D_i\Psi_s^\ell(\Phi_s)\sigma_s^{i\nu}(\Phi_s)&=0,\\
 \beta_s^\ell(\Phi_s)+D_i\Psi_s^\ell(\Phi_s)b_s^i(\Phi_s)
 +\tfrac12a_s^{ip}(\Phi_s)D_{ip}\Psi_s^\ell(\Phi_s)
 +\sum_{\nu=1}^rD_i\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}(\Phi_s)
                  \sigma_s^{i\nu}(\Phi_s)&=0.
 \end{align*}
Substitution of
\[
 D_i\zeta_s^{\ell\nu}
 =-D_{ip}\Psi_s^\ell\sigma_s^{p\nu}
  -D_p\Psi_s^\ell D_i\sigma_s^{p\nu}
\]
proves \eqref{eq:inverse-flow-diffusion}-\eqref{eq:inverse-flow-drift}.

We now justify the passage from the classical smooth
It\^o--Wentzell formula to the localized Sobolev setting.  Fix $R<M$ and $j\ge1$.  Let
$\vartheta=\vartheta_{j,R,M}$ be the minimum of $\theta$,
$\kappa_j^{M+2}$ from \eqref{eq:IW-local-Sobolev-norms}, the time when
$\Psi_s(B_R)$ leaves $B_M$, and the time when
$\|\Psi_s\|_{C^2(B_R)}+\|\det D\Psi_s\|_{C(B_R)}
 +\|(\det D\Psi_s)^{-1}\|_{C(B_R)}$ exceeds $M$.  Here, for $k=0,1,2$, we write
 \[
 \|f\|_{C^k(B_R)}
 :=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\sup_{x\in B_R}|D^\alpha f(x)|,
 \]
 with $C^0(B_R)=C(B_R)$.
 
  Choose
$
 0<\delta<\min\left\{1,n_*-2-\frac d2\right\}$ and define 
$ V^{\varepsilon,M}:=\varrho_\varepsilon*(\chi_MV),
 V\in\{U,A,B,C\},
$
where $\chi_M\in C_c^\infty(B_{M+2})$ satisfies
$\chi_M=1$ on $B_{M+1}$, and
$\varrho_\varepsilon(x):=\varepsilon^{-d}\varrho(x/\varepsilon)$
for a fixed nonnegative function $\varrho\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$
with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varrho(x)\,\mathrm{d}x=1$.
 
For $0<\varepsilon<1$, the standard
mollifier estimate and Sobolev embeddings
\citep[Chapter~4]{AdamsFournier2003} give
\begin{align*}
 \|U_s^{\varepsilon,M}-U_s\|_{C^2(B_M)}
 &\le C_M\varepsilon^\delta\|U_s\|_{H^{n_*}(B_{M+2})},\\
 \|A_s^{\varepsilon,M}-A_s\|_{C(B_M)}
 &\le C_M\varepsilon^\delta\|A_s\|_{H^{n_*-2}(B_{M+2})},\\
 \|B_s^{\varepsilon,M}-B_s\|_{C(B_M)}
 &\le C_M\varepsilon^\delta
   \|B_s\|_{H^{n_*-1}(B_{M+2})},\\
 \|C_s^{\varepsilon,M}-C_s\|_{C^1(B_M)}
 &\le C_M\varepsilon^\delta
   \|C_s\|_{H^{n_*-1}(B_{M+2})}.
\end{align*}
Hence, by \eqref{eq:IW-local-Sobolev-norms}, as $\varepsilon \to 0$, we have  
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\le\vartheta}
   \|U_s^{\varepsilon,M}-U_s\|_{C^2(B_M)}^2
 +\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\vartheta
   \|A_s^{\varepsilon,M}-A_s\|_{C(B_M)}\,\mathrm d s
 \notag\\
 &\quad+\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\vartheta
 \left(\|B_s^{\varepsilon,M}-B_s\|_{C(B_M)}^2
 +\|C_s^{\varepsilon,M}-C_s\|_{C^1(B_M)}^2\right)\,\mathrm d s
 \longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:IW-mollification-limit}
\end{align}

Applying the classical formula
\citep[Theorem~3.1]{Krylov2011} to
$U_s^{\varepsilon,M}(\Psi_s(x))$ yields
\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-formula} with $U$ replaced by
$U^{\varepsilon,M}$ and coefficients
$\widehat A^{\varepsilon,M}$, $\widehat B^{\varepsilon,M}$,
and $\widehat C^{\varepsilon,M}$, obtained by substituting
the mollified fields into
\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-drift}--\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-W}.


On the stochastic interval $[0,\vartheta]$, the composition map
$f\mapsto f\circ\Psi_s$ is bounded from $C^q(B_M)$ to
$C^q(B_R)$, uniformly in $s$, for $q=0,1,2$, and
\[
 \sup_{x\in B_R}(|\beta_s(x)|+|\zeta_s(x)|^2)
 \le C_{R,M}(1+|u_s|^2),\qquad
 \int_0^\theta(1+|u_s|^2)\,\mathrm d s\le T+k.
\]
Thus, \eqref{eq:IW-mollification-limit}, Cauchy--Schwarz, and BDG give:
for $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B_R)$,
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\vartheta
  |\langle\widehat A_s^{\varepsilon,M}-\widehat A_s,
          \varphi\rangle|\,\mathrm d s&\longrightarrow0,\\
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{0\le q\le\vartheta}\left|
  \int_0^q\langle\widehat B_s^{\varepsilon,M}-\widehat B_s,
          \varphi\rangle^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s
 +\sum_{\nu=1}^r\int_0^q
  \langle\widehat C_s^{\varepsilon,M,\nu}-\widehat C_s^\nu,
          \varphi\rangle\,\mathrm d W_s^\nu\right|^2
 &\longrightarrow0.
\end{align*}
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves
\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-formula}-\eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-W}.  The same localization and mollification argument with $\Phi_{t,s}$
proves \eqref{eq:forward-flow-IW}.



Fix $R<\infty$, for each fixed integer $M>R$, condition
$\mathrm{(IW)}_{n_*}$ gives
\[
\kappa_j^{M+2}\uparrow\theta
\qquad\text{as }j\to\infty,\quad\mathbb Q\text{-a.s.}
\]
Thus, letting $j\to\infty$ removes the localization imposed by
$\kappa_j^{M+2}$.

Next, the inverse-flow regularity in Lemma~\ref{98} implies that
\[
\sup_{s\le\theta}\|\Psi_s\|_{C^2(B_R)}
+\sup_{s\le\theta}\bigl(
\|\det D\Psi_s\|_{C(B_R)}
+\|(\det D\Psi_s)^{-1}\|_{C(B_R)}
\bigr)<\infty
\qquad\mathbb Q\text{-a.s.}
\]
Consequently, for almost every sample path, all sufficiently large
$M$ ensure that $\Psi_s(B_R)\subset B_M$ and that the above norms
remain below $M$ throughout $[0,\theta]$. Hence
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\lim_{j\to\infty}
\vartheta_{j,R,M}=\theta
\qquad\mathbb Q\text{-a.s.}
\]
This removes the localizations, continuity extends the identities
to the terminal time $\theta$ and completes the proof.

For the inverse formula, stochastic Fubini
\citep[Lemma~2.6]{Krylov2011}, a countable dense family of test
functions, and continuity in the test function and time yield
the asserted common full-probability event.

For the forward formula at fixed $t$, Fubini's theorem and
continuity in time yield a common full-probability event on which
the identity holds for almost every starting point,
simultaneously for all times.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $N$ and define, for $0\le s\le\theta$ and $y\in\mathbb R^d$,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		U_s(y):=F_s^{N,0,y},
		A_s(y):=-(H_s^{N,0,y})^\top G_s^{N,0,y},
		B_s(y):=G_s^{N,0,y},
		C_s(y):=\widetilde G_s^{N,0,y}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	We first verify condition $\mathrm{(IW)}_{n_*}$.
For every $M<\infty$, Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-parameter}
	and Fubini's theorem give
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\le\theta}
	\|U_s\|_{H^{n_*}(B_M)}^2
	+\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta
	\left(
	\|B_s\|_{H^{n_*-1}(B_M)}^2
	+\|C_s\|_{H^{n_*-1}(B_M)}^2
	\right)\mathrm{d}s<\infty.
	\]
From Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-estimates}, we have 
	\[
	\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^d}
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\le\theta}
	|D_y^\eta H_s^{N,0,y}|^4<\infty,
	\qquad |\eta|\le n_*-2.
	\]
Therefore,	by the product rule, Cauchy--Schwarz, and
	Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-parameter} with $q=4$,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta
		\|A_s\|_{H^{n_*-2}(B_M)}^2\,\mathrm{d}s\\
		&\quad\le
		C\sum_{|\alpha|\le n_*-2}\sum_{\eta\le\alpha}
		\int_{B_M}
		\left(
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\le\theta}
		|D_y^\eta H_s^{N,0,y}|^4
		\right)^{1/2}\\
		&\qquad\qquad\qquad\times
		\left[
		\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\left(
		\int_0^\theta
		|D_y^{\alpha-\eta}G_s^{N,0,y}|^2\,\mathrm{d}s
		\right)^2
		\right]^{1/2}\,\mathrm{d}y
		<\infty.
	\end{aligned}
	\]

	Moreover, pairing \eqref{eq:truncated-BSDE} with a test
	function and applying stochastic Fubini gives
	\eqref{eq:generic-parameter-semimartingale} in the weak
	spatial sense. Thus $(U,A,B,C)$ satisfies
	$\mathrm{(IW)}_{n_*}$.
	
	We may therefore apply the inverse formula in
	Lemma~\ref{lem:flow-composition}. Since
	\[
	U_s(\Psi_s(x))=f_s^N(x),
	\qquad B_s(\Psi_s(x))=g_s^N(x),
	\]
	we obtain
	\begin{align}
		\mathrm{d}f_s^N(x)
		=
		A_s^N(x)\,\mathrm{d}s
		+(g_s^N(x))^\top\,\mathrm{d}Y_s
		+(q_s^N(x))^\top\,\mathrm{d}W_s,
		\label{eq:preliminary-eulerian-decomp}
			\end{align}
			where
				\begin{align}
		q_s^{N,\nu}(x)
		=
		\widetilde G_s^{N,0,\Psi_s(x),\nu}
		-\sum_{i=1}^d
		D_i f_s^N(x)\sigma^{i\nu}(x,u_s),
		\qquad \nu=1,\ldots,r.
		\label{eq:q-explicit}
	\end{align}
	Here $A_s^N(x)$ denotes the drift $\widehat A_s(x)$
	defined by \eqref{eq:inverse-pullback-drift}
	for the above choices of $(U,A,B,C)$.

Choose a countable set $\mathcal D\subset C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$
such that $\mathcal D\cap C_c^\infty(B_R)$ is dense in
$L^2(B_R)$ for every integer $R\ge1$. Define 
$Z_t^{N,\varphi}=\langle f_{t\wedge\theta}^N,\varphi\rangle$.
By Proposition  \ref{prop:diagonal-Y} and Stricker's theorem
\citep[Theorem~2.1]{FollmerProtter2011}, $Z^{N,\varphi}$ is a
$\mathbb G^k$-semimartingale.  By Lemma 
\ref{lem:reference-stopping-functional}, its local martingale part is a
$Y_{\cdot\wedge\theta}$-integral, and is orthogonal to
$W$.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 0=[Z^{N,\varphi},W^\nu]_t
 =\int_0^{t\wedge\theta}
   \langle q_s^{N,\nu},\varphi\rangle\,\mathrm d s,
 \label{eq:q-bracket-zero}
\end{equation}
so density of $\mathcal D$ gives
\[
 q^N=0\qquad
 \text{in }\,\mathrm d\mathbb Q\otimes\,\mathrm d s\otimes\,\mathrm d x.
\]

Let $K^{N,\varphi}$ denote the $\mathbb G^k$-predictable
integrand in the $Y_{\cdot\wedge\theta}$-representation of
the local martingale part of $Z^{N,\varphi}$.
Computing $[Z^{N,\varphi},Y^j]$ from
\eqref{eq:preliminary-eulerian-decomp} and from this
representation gives
\[
\int_0^{t\wedge\theta}
\langle g_s^{N,j},\varphi\rangle\,\mathrm{d}s
=[Z^{N,\varphi},Y^j]_t
=\int_0^{t\wedge\theta}
K_s^{N,\varphi,j}\,\mathrm{d}s,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Therefore, for all $t\in[0,T]$,
\[
\langle g_s^{N,j},\varphi\rangle=K_s^{N,\varphi,j}
\qquad
\mathrm{d}\mathbb Q\otimes\mathrm{d}s\text{-a.e. on }[0,\theta].
\]
Thus each pairing $\langle g_s^{N,j},\varphi\rangle$
admits a $\mathbb G^k$-predictable version.

 For an orthonormal basis
$(e_i^R)_{i\ge1}\subset\mathcal D$ of $L^2(B_R)$, Parseval's identity
gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^J
 \langle g_s^{N},e_i^R\rangle e_i^R
 \longrightarrow g_s^N
 \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega\times[0,\theta]\times B_R).
\]
Closedness of the predictable subspace yields a $\mathbb G^k$-predictable
version of $g^N$, and \eqref{eq:local-g-strong} gives the same conclusion for
$g$.

Since $q^N=0$, the forward formula in Lemma 
\ref{lem:flow-composition} yields
\begin{align*}
 \,\mathrm d F_s^{N,0,y}
 ={}&[A_s^N+L_sf_s^N](\Phi_s(y))\,\mathrm d s
 +g_s^N(\Phi_s(y))^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s\\
 &+[\sigma(\Phi_s(y),u_s)^\top
       \nabla f_s^N(\Phi_s(y))]^\top\,\mathrm d W_s.
\end{align*}
Comparison with \eqref{eq:truncated-BSDE}  gives
\[
 A_s^N=-L_sf_s^N-h_N(\cdot,u_s)^\top g_s^N,\qquad
 \widetilde G_s^{N,0,y}
 =\sigma(\Phi_s(y),u_s)^\top\nabla f_s^N(\Phi_s(y)).
\]
Moreover, by \eqref{eq:reconstruct-N} and  \eqref{eq:truncated-BSDE}, we have 
\[
f_\theta^N(\Phi_\theta(y))
=F_\theta^{N,0,y}
=\gamma(X_\theta^{0,y})
=\gamma(\Phi_\theta(y)),
\qquad y\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
Since $\Phi_\theta$ is a diffeomorphism with inverse
$\Psi_\theta$, taking $y=\Psi_\theta(x)$ gives
\[
f_\theta^N(x)
=\gamma(x),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.
\]
Combining above, we finish the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B_R)$.   The weak form of
\eqref{eq:truncated-BSPDE} is
\begin{align}
 \left\langle f_{t\wedge\theta}^N,\varphi\right\rangle
 ={}&\left\langle \gamma,\varphi\right\rangle
 +\int_{t\wedge\theta}^{\theta}\left\langle f_s^N,L_s^*\varphi\right\rangle\,\mathrm d s
 \notag\\
 &+\int_{t\wedge\theta}^{\theta}
    \left\langle h_N(\cdot,u_s)^\top g_s^N,\varphi\right\rangle\,\mathrm d s
 -\int_{t\wedge\theta}^{\theta}\left\langle g_s^N,\varphi\right\rangle^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s.
 \label{eq:weak-N}
\end{align}
The convergence of its four terms follows from
\eqref{eq:local-f-strong}--\eqref{eq:local-g-strong}.  More precisely,
the coefficient assumptions give
\[
 \|L_s^*\varphi\|_{L^2(B_R)}
 \le C_{\varphi,R}(1+|u_s|^2),
\]
and therefore
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta
 |\langle f_s^N-f_s,L_s^*\varphi\rangle|\,\mathrm d s
 &\le C_{\varphi,R}(T+k)
 \left(\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{s\le\theta}
       \|f_s^N-f_s\|_{L^2(B_R)}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{align*}
Note that 
\begin{align*}
	&\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
	\left|
	h_N(x,u_s)^\top g_s^N(x)
	-h(x,u_s)^\top g_s(x)
	\right|\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}s\\
	&\quad\le
	\left(
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
	|h_N(x,u_s)-h(x,u_s)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}s
	\right)^{1/2}\\
	&\qquad\quad\times
	\left(
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
	|g_s^N(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}s
	\right)^{1/2}\\
	&\qquad+
	\left(
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
	|h(x,u_s)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}s
	\right)^{1/2}\\
	&\qquad\quad\times
	\left(
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
	|g_s^N(x)-g_s(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}s
	\right)^{1/2}
	\longrightarrow0.
\end{align*}

Finally, BDG gives
\begin{align*}
 &\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{0\le t\le T}
 \left|\int_0^{t\wedge\theta}
   \langle g_s^N-g_s,\varphi\rangle^\top\,\mathrm d Y_s\right|^2\\
 &\qquad\le C\|\varphi\|_{L^2(B_R)}^2
   \mathbb E^\mathbb Q\int_0^\theta\int_{B_R}
      |g_s^N(x)-g_s(x)|^2\,\mathrm d x\,\mathrm d s
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{align*}
Passing to the limit in \eqref{eq:weak-N} yields
\eqref{eq:weak-bspde}, $\mathbb Q$-almost surely, for each fixed
$t\in[0,T]$ and $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$.
Taking countable dense sets of times and test functions,
and using continuity in time and in the test function,
we obtain a common event of probability one on which
this identity holds simultaneously for all $t\in[0,T]$

label: lem:maximal-lsc
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:maximal-lsc}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a separable Hilbert space and $\theta\le T$ a stopping time.  On $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T);\mathcal H)$ define
\[
 \mathfrak J(v)
 :=\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0\le s\le\theta}\left\lVert v_s\right\rVert_{\mathcal H}^2,
\]
with value $+\infty$ when the right-hand side is infinite.  Then $\mathfrak J$ is convex and weakly lower semicontinuous.

name: Lower semicontinuity of the maximal Hilbert norm

label: cc
title: Proof
body_md:
Convexity is immediate.  Suppose  $v^j\to v$
strongly in $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T);\mathcal H)$, if 
$
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\mathfrak J(v^j) =+\infty,
$ 
the desired inequality is immediate.
Otherwise choose a subsequence  $(v^{j_k})$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{cc}
\mathfrak J(v^{j_k})\longrightarrow \liminf_{j\to\infty}\mathfrak J(v^j) .
\end{equation}
Strong $L^2$ convergence allows us to extract a further
subsequence, still denoted by $(v^{j_k})$, for which
\[
\|v_s^{j_k}(\omega)-v_s(\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}
\longrightarrow0
\qquad
\text{for }\mathrm{d}\mathbb Q\otimes\mathrm{d}s
\text{-a.e. }(\omega,s).
\]
and  the convergence \eqref{cc} is preserved
under this further extraction.

By Fubini's theorem, for $\mathbb Q$-a.e.\ $\omega$, this convergence
holds for Lebesgue-a.e.\ $s\in(0,T)$.
For each such $\omega$,  we have 
\[
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0<s\le\theta(\omega)}
\|v_s(\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}^2
\le
\liminf_{k\to\infty}
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0<s\le\theta(\omega)}
\|v_s^{j_k}(\omega)\|_{\mathcal H}^2.
\]
Consequently, Fatou's lemma yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
	\mathfrak J(v)
	&\le
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\!\left[
	\liminf_{k\to\infty}
	\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0<s\le\theta}
	\|v_s^{j_k}\|_{\mathcal H}^2
	\right]\\
	&\le
	\liminf_{k\to\infty}\mathfrak J(v^{j_k})
	=\liminf_{j\to\infty}\mathfrak J(v^j).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus $\mathfrak J$ is lower semicontinuous in the norm topology.
Since it is also convex, it is weakly lower semicontinuous
by \citet[Corollary~3.9, p.~61]{Brezis2011}.

head: environment
name: Boundedness of the first component

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:FN-representation},
$|F_r^{N,0,y}|\le \|\gamma\|_\infty$ for rational $(r,y)$.
	Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-parameter} and Kolmogorov's continuity
	theorem yield versions jointly continuous in $(s,y)$.
	Taking a countable intersection over $N$ and rational $(r,y)$,
	and then using continuity, gives
	\[
	|F_s^{N,0,y}|\le \|\gamma\|_\infty
	\quad\text{for all }N\in\mathbb N,\ s\in[0,T],\ y\in\mathbb R^d
	\]
	on a common event of probability one. Consequently,
	\[
	|f_s^N(x)|=|F_s^{N,0,\Psi_s(x)}|\le \|\gamma\|_\infty
	\quad\text{for all }N\in\mathbb N,\ 0\le s\le\theta,\ x\in\mathbb R^d.
	\]

 Since
	$(|f_s(x)|-\|\gamma\|_\infty)_+\le |f_s(x)-f_s^N(x)|$,
	\eqref{eq:local-f-strong} gives
	\[
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{s\le\theta}
	\bigl\|(|f_s|-\|\gamma\|_\infty)_+\bigr\|_{L^2(B_R)}^2
	\le
	\mathbb E^\mathbb Q\sup_{s\le\theta}
	\|f_s^N-f_s\|_{L^2(B_R)}^2
	\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	Hence, almost surely,
	\[
	\bigl\|(|f_s|-\|\gamma\|_\infty)_+\bigr\|_{L^2(B_R)}=0
	\qquad\text{for every }s\le\theta.
	\]
	
	By spatial continuity of $f_s$, for each integer
	$R\ge1$ there is an event $\Omega_R$ with $\mathbb Q(\Omega_R)=1$
	such that
	\[
	|f_s(\omega,x)|\le\|\gamma\|_\infty
	\quad\text{for every }\omega\in\Omega_R,\ 
	0\le s\le\theta(\omega),\ x\in B_R.
	\]
	Set $\Omega_0:=\bigcap_{R=1}^{\infty}\Omega_R$.
	Then $\mathbb Q(\Omega_0)=1$, and the bound holds on $\Omega_0$
	for every $s\le\theta$ and $x\in\mathbb R^d$, since
	$\bigcup_{R=1}^{\infty}B_R=\mathbb R^d$.
	This proves \eqref{eq:f-bound-common-version}.
